Last week after Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta 1, Bitrig has also added support for building and testing iPhone Duo applications, and is equipped with an interactive 3D simulator, allowing developers to freely fold, tilt, rotate and position the device. The details are as follows.

Bitrig now lets users try out a 3D iPhone Duo

Bitrig originally launched as a simple vibe-coding application, allowing users to convert text or voice prompts into native SwiftUI applications that run directly within the Bitrig main app on iPhone.

Since then, the platform has expanded significantly, adding a Mac application that allows users to use the full Xcode toolchain, an integrated iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and the ability to export projects to Xcode or publish applications via TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, along with Apple's release of Xcode 27.1 beta 1 which supports building and testing iPhone Duo applications, Bitrig also launched its own support for iPhone Duo, reinterpreting the simulator in a more interactive way.

Here is Bitrig co-founder and CEO Kyle Macomber explaining the features brought by this update:

Try out all kinds of postures. The iPhone Duo can be placed flat on a desk like a laptop, or stood on a bedside table like a tent. Whether opened, folded, or half-folded, whether portrait or landscape, your application needs to respond flexibly. Bitrig's 3D simulator lets you grab, fold, and rotate the device at will, observing in real time how your application responds. Responding to hinge movements. Use onHingeChange to drive interactive effects when the phone is folded, such as the Apple unfold effect that makes the outer screen feel like a window into the inner screen. Freely open and close it in the built-in simulator to read hinge data in real time. Create hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to arrange the upper half to display media content and the lower half to place control interfaces, convenient for use when the iPhone Duo is placed flat on a desk. Support for landscape display orientation allows users to stand the device on its side when using your application on the outer screen. Use both screens simultaneously. Add CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer screen to provide useful visual information for the person facing the camera.

Macomber also mentioned: "Bitrig helps you manage multiple Xcode versions, so you can first use the beta version to start preparing your application for iPhone Duo, then switch back to Xcode 27 at any time to build and publish updates."
